title: Rename a macro
summary: Renaming a macro edits its `#define` in each branch of the `#if` it is defined in, the `#ifndef` guarding a default, and every use, written as another macro's argument or in another macro's body; a use pasted together with `##` is left alone and named in a message

files.text:
#pragma once

#ifndef BUFFER_SIZE
#define BUFFER_SIZE 64
#endif

#ifdef SMALL_BUFFERS
#define LIMIT 16
#else
#define LIMIT 256
#endif

#define TWICE(n) ((n) * 2)
#define CLAMP(n) ((n) < LIMIT ? (n) : LIMIT)
#define APPLY(f, n) f(n)
#define CAT(a, b) a##b

rename.notice:
Spellings of `BUFFER_SIZE` left alone:
  ${WS}/main.cpp:6: int pasted = CAT(BUFFER_, SIZE); (the name is written here as `CAT`)

edits.config.h:
#ifdef SMALL_BUFFERS
-#define LIMIT 16
+#define MAX_LIMIT 16
 #else
-#define LIMIT 256
+#define MAX_LIMIT 256
 #endif

 #define TWICE(n) ((n) * 2)
-#define CLAMP(n) ((n) < LIMIT ? (n) : LIMIT)
+#define CLAMP(n) ((n) < MAX_LIMIT ? (n) : MAX_LIMIT)
 #define APPLY(f, n) f(n)
 #define CAT(a, b) a##b

#endif

-#define TWICE(n) ((n) * 2)
+#define DOUBLE(n) ((n) * 2)
 #define CLAMP(n) ((n) < LIMIT ? (n) : LIMIT)
 #define APPLY(f, n) f(n)
